claim: For the real hexagonal plane \(X_\gamma=(\mathbb R^2,N_\gamma)\), \(N_\gamma(x,y)=\max\{|y|,\ |x|+(1-\gamma)|y|\}\), one has \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X_\gamma)=2/(1+\gamma)\) for every \(0<\gamma<1/2\).

correctness.rationale: The source definition and six extreme points were checked directly. The proof establishes the global comparison \(H_\gamma\le N_\gamma\le \sqrt{2/(1+\gamma)}H_\gamma\) for every \(0<\gamma<1/2\), applies the Hilbert Ptolemy inequality, and matches the resulting upper bound with an explicit three-point configuration whose required norms are evaluated exactly.

value.rationale: The Ptolemy constant is a standard invariant linked to Banach-space geometry and normal structure, and the source family is a named one-parameter hexagonal test family used for exact geometric constants. The cutoff \(\gamma=1/2\) is mathematically intrinsic to the sharp Hilbert comparison. The result therefore determines a natural full nontrivial regime rather than an arbitrary slice.
